articles.title: The double risk of low-cost online marketplaces reaching Spain
articles.dek: A small per-parcel charge on low-value imports is an insufficient patch for a much bigger problem: domestic retailers competing against a wave of ultra-cheap goods with little regulatory oversight.
articles.author: THE EDITORIAL BOARD
body: The government's proposed charge on low-value parcels is a reasonable first step, but it treats the symptom rather than the underlying imbalance. Ultra-cheap online marketplaces have built their model on shipping small, individually-taxed packages directly to consumers, sidestepping the customs and compliance costs that domestic retailers absorb as a matter of course.

A flat per-parcel fee will raise some revenue and modestly narrow the price gap, but it does nothing to address product safety standards, labour conditions in supplier factories, or the environmental cost of shipping millions of single items by air freight.
Spain, like much of the EU, now has to decide whether it wants a durable framework for this kind of trade or a patchwork of reactive charges that arrive a decade too late.
